newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude ends just above new three-week low.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude ends just above new three-week low.

text.p: IPE Brent crude ended just above a three-week low on Tuesday, closing over 60 cents down as funds took their cue from bearish chart signals, dealers said.
Brent spent much of the early part of the session treading water just below Monday's close but a weak opening in New York generated by independent floor traders quickly gathered pace.
"There was trade selling of the spreads and outright price and as the market hit new lows it attracted heavier fund activity," said a broker.
July Brent closed 62 cents down at $18.90 a barrel, just above the intraday low of $18.88, a level last seen on May 9.

NYMEX July crude's break through support at $20.55 generated a technical sell-off in London. July Brent breached an imperfect double bottom at $19.09-$19.10 before finally coming to rest above a gap between $18.80 and $18.88 left in early May.
Dealers said market sentiment took a knock from expectations of a small rise in U.S. crude stocks which are already running some 18 million barrels ahead of year ago levels.

American Petroleum Institute (API) data due to be released later on Tuesday should show crude stocks rose by between 300,000 and 1.4 million barrels last week as imports continued to flood into the U.S. Gulf, according to a Reuter survey.
News that the U.S. had given its backing to the renewal of the U.N. oil-for-food deal with Iraq also added to the bearish backdrop, dealers said.
U.N. Security Council members are scheduled to meet on Tuesday to draft a resolution to allow the pact's renewal. A vote could be taken as early as Wednesday, U.N. officials said.
Earlier, IPE gas oil also ended sharply lower, June shedding $4 to close at $170.00 a tonne.
The prompt contango widened by a further 25 cents to $1.50 as the July contract finished at $171.50.
